record.context_brief: Systematic construction of equienergetic non-cospectral trees
record.original_question: Let the energy of a graph be the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. Two graphs of the same order are called equienergetic if they have the same energy, and they are called non-cospectral if their adjacency spectra are different. Construct a systematic method for producing a pair of trees on the same number of vertices that are both equienergetic and non-cospectral.

evidence.quote: (1) Construct at a pair of non-cospectral equienergetic trees.
(1) Although it is known that there are numerous pairs of equienergetic, non-cospectral trees, it is not known how to systematically construct any such pair.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple graph with adjacency matrix A(G). The energy of G is defined as
    E(G) = sum_{i=1}^{n} |λ_i|,
where λ_1, …, λ_n are the eigenvalues of A(G). Two graphs of the same order are called equienergetic if E(G) = E(H), and non-cospectral if their multisets of adjacency eigenvalues differ.

Provide a systematic construction (i.e., an explicit infinite family or a general procedure depending on parameters) that, given input parameters, produces a pair (T_1, T_2) of trees on the same number of vertices such that T_1 and T_2 are equienergetic and non-cospectral.
artifact.status_search_result: Sporadic pairs of equienergetic non-cospectral trees are known (smallest examples on 9, 14, 15 vertices), and there is work on "equienergetic and almost-equienergetic trees" by Gutman et al. (MATCH 61 (2009), 451–461). Systematic constructions are well known for general graphs (e.g., via iterated line graphs of regular graphs), but the line-graph technique does not apply to trees, and no fully general systematic construction of equienergetic non-cospectral tree pairs appears in the literature; the problem seems still partially open.

status_evidence.title: Equienergetic and almost-equienergetic trees
status_evidence.snippet: Equienergetic and almost-equienergetic trees, MATCH Commun. Math. Comput. Chem. 61 (2009) 451-461.
status_evidence.claim: Work exists studying equienergetic and almost-equienergetic trees, indicating only partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Equienergetic chemical trees
status_evidence.snippet: Smallest pairs of non-cospectral equienergetic chemical trees on 9, 14, 15 vertices are identified.
status_evidence.claim: Specific small examples are known, but no fully general systematic construction for trees is provided.

status_evidence.title: Constructing pairs of equienergetic and non-cospectral graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Systematic constructions of equienergetic non-cospectral graphs using iterated line graphs and graph products.
status_evidence.claim: Known systematic constructions for general graphs use line graphs, which do not produce trees.
